figure_legends: Figure 1. Rankings under association-constant weights (x-axis) against the baseline-subtracted log-affinity form (y-axis, median rank over the baseline sweep), on Davis and Klaeger. Top: entropy, for which association-constant weights are the published form. Bottom: Gini, shown for comparison. Its published form uses percent inhibition. Grey: floor-coded pairs kept at the floor. Blue: floor-coded pairs given zero weight. Spearman r above each panel.

Figure 2. Binding profiles of two Davis compounds, targets sorted by affinity. Left: fedratinib, the most ratio-sensitive compound, with JAK2 and GAK tied among 123 active targets. Right: PHA-665752, the most unstable compound overall (σ=16.4), with one dominant target among 60 active targets. Dashed line: pKd=6 activity threshold. Dotted line: pKd=5 coded floor.

Figure 3. Recovery from random subpanels with D1 applied to every score, on all four datasets (50 subpanels per size). Top: coverage, the share of compounds scored on the full panel that are still scored. Middle: recoverability, the share of clearly separated full-panel pairs that are scored on the subpanel and keep their order. Bottom: mean Spearman correlation between subpanel and full-panel rankings over compounds scored on both, with ±1 standard deviation across subpanels shaded. Each score is compared with its own full-panel ranking. The published entropy and Pmax give floor-coded pairs zero weight and are not defined on Anastassiadis. Dashed line: 0.90.
